summary: The feature correctly rebrands the public CLI, public deep-link scheme, and release-facing local paths, but the Linux uninstall flow does not remove the actual per-channel IPC socket filename that the runtime creates.

issues.description: The Linux uninstall script removes `~/.local/share/neozed/neozed-$db_suffix.sock`, but the CLI/runtime create per-channel sockets named `zed-<channel>.sock`, so uninstall leaves the stale IPC socket behind.
issues.evidence: `crates/cli/src/main.rs` and `crates/zed/src/zed/open_listener.rs` both build socket paths with `format!("zed-{}.sock", RELEASE_CHANNEL_NAME)`, while `script/uninstall.sh` removes `~/.local/share/neozed/neozed-$db_suffix.sock`.
